title: Three beats in a bar: Always With Me

blocks.text:
The theme from *Spirited Away* is a waltz: three beats in each bar, not four.

**By the end** you can count and tap music in 3/4 and play the first eight bars with both hands.

blocks.caption: Always With Me, from Spirited Away (a PDMX arrangement). ▶ to hear it.

blocks.text:
# 3/4 time
**3/4** means three quarter-note beats in a bar: count 1 2 3, 1 2 3, with the weight on 1. A **dotted half note** fills a whole bar of 3/4.

The tune uses eighths, quarters and one **dotted quarter** in bar 3: a beat and a half, held over the second beat.

blocks.title: The tune's rhythm
blocks.doneWhen: 4 of the 6 cards clean in one set

blocks.title: More in 3/4
blocks.about: Read in time: dotted halves and 3/4, made up fresh.

blocks.text:
# The tune
The tune starts on beat 3 of bar 2 and stays between middle C and the C above: C D E F G A, and C at the top. It starts **F G A F C**: up by steps, then a leap of a 5th up to C.

blocks.title: The tune, right hand
blocks.about: Wait for me, right hand, bars 2–8.

blocks.text:
# The waltz left hand
Every bar of the left hand goes **low note, chord, chord**: "oom-pah-pah". In bar 1 the low note is the **F** just below the bass staff, then the chord **F A C** twice.

blocks.title: The waltz left hand
blocks.about: Wait for me, left hand, bars 1–4.

blocks.text:
# If this happens
- **You count four.** Say "1 2 3" out loud for a bar before starting.
- **The left hand's jump is late.** Move on beat 3, as the second chord ends.

**Until the next lesson:** the eight bars once a day.
